name: 10×10 board (baseline)
body: 10×10 board accepted as baseline after P1 confirmed size felt right for both players.

name: 3 HP for Champions/King (Guards stay 2 HP)
body: Would extend game (first Champion kill at R26 with 2 HP). Guards at 2 HP vs Champions at 3 HP creates artificial tier.

name: 3rd skill slot per Champion
body: 2 slots forces specialist builds; 3 risks generalist meta. Fix for 'narrow variety' is better skill design, not more slots.

name: Armor cap 3→2 + Plate +1→+2 (bundled) - Stack H
body: Reduces chassis-loop volume (Framing B alignment); Plate becomes one-shot fortify rather than stack-grind. P4 confirmed Q-C1 chassis-volume hypothesis. Session 25: ABSORBED INTO STACK M - only the cap-2 component, not Plate +2. Stack H exists as isolation-fallback only.

name: Defense / Armor's role - diagnosis: late-game survival tax
body: Three diagnoses tested for the late-game Armor problem. A (Money curve too steep): KILLED. B (HP too thin): KILLED. C (Armor's shape is wrong, functions as late-game survival tax / mandatory upkeep): CONFIRMED. User verbatim: 'i 100% agree that armor is like the tax you have to pay.' Diagnosis anchor - not a candidate fix.

name: Ban phase in draft
body: From older game version with unique fixed-skill Champions. Needs 20+ skills and a different draft model.

name: Board 8×8 with fewer pieces
body: Decoupled Session 22: 8×8 lives in Stack D (Board Geometry); piece count reduction lives in Stack K. Test independently. Note: 8×8 absorbed into Stack M.

name: Bodyguard: adjacent to defender only; Guard takes damage (Stack B)
body: Session 22 (2026-05-29). P4 confirmed Bodyguard tracks standoff state, not the rule (0 triggers when Armor stalling returned). Defender-only adjacency unlikely to be the right fix.

name: Bodyguard intercepts Move-Attacks only, not skills
body: Skills always hit directly. Session 3 ruling.

name: Breakthrough bonus (+1 Slot on first Champion hit)
body: Subsumed into cascade trigger; arbitrary 'first hit' trigger less elegant.

name: Cascade trigger (+1 action on kill)
body: Anti-snowball one-turn tempo bonus on kill. Backpocket; test in Stack F.

name: Champion pre-naming (Blacksmith, Necromancer, etc.)
body: Champions are blank slates - identity emerges from equipped skills.

name: Checkmate-style win condition
body: Verification burden too high - too many defensive options (heal, armor, push, LoS block) to prove '100% lost' at the table.

name: Class-based skill pools (Champion's class determines drafting)
body: Restricts strategy freedom for minimal complexity reduction. Contradicts blank-slate Champion design.

name: Collision damage (universal push-into-piece = 1 damage)
body: Conditional on standoff resolution.

name: Multi-Champion Combo Bonus migrated into baseline
body: Concise version of the rule promoted into `section-multi-champion-combo()` - and added as a row in the quick-reference table. Niko (P4 first-time player) skipped reading the long version and still understood the rule, proving the dense version is sufficient. Worked examples + tracking tables stay out of baseline. BASELINE_VERSION bumped 2026-05-26 → 2026-05-30.

name: Multi-Champion combo bonus - Strike-only, single-counter (Stack A G2)
body: +1 damage on 2nd+ Strike hit when 2+ different Champions target same enemy this turn. Stack A G2 data was mixed: confirmed in mechanics, weak in feel. Session 22 reframe: Q3 softness is design-aligned (few-times-a-game payoff). Lever is scope, not strength.

name: Combo bonus dual-counter + widened scope (Stack A G3)
body: Two parallel counters per turn: target counter (different friendly Champions hitting same enemy) + attacker counter (same friendly Champion hitting different enemy targets). Any skill that hits an enemy piece counts (not Strike-only). Multi-target ticks all hits. Move-Attacks excluded. Both counters stack. Justification: cross-category crowd-out, late-game offensive lockout, exchange-pit pattern. Methodology: gated behind Stack H so chassis trim lands first.

name: Coordinated movement bonus (−1 Money if pieces move to same zone)
body: Too easy to trigger accidentally; doesn't reward cleverness.

name: CR-style draft picks (strict interleaving)
body: Restricts free strategy with small catalogue. Variant material.

name: Cross-pole shared fix - per-pole-revival (not once-and-carry)
body: P5 confirmed Armor 3 feels mandatory in both Pole A (P4) and Pole B (P5). Designer's lean was 'twice for cleanness.' With Pole B paused, Stack H runs in Pole A only. If Pole B is ever revived, Stack H (or its successor) runs again there. Carry-forward is per-pole-revival, not once-and-carry.

name: Damage escalation after Round X
body: Only if games are still 25+ rounds after Stacks A–C.

name: Default Skill Range = 2 (Range 0=self, 1=adjacent, 2=2 tiles)
body: Now defined in all rule sheets. P2 mid-game ruling.

name: Defender chooses which Guard intercepts
body: P1 suggestion accepted as ruling.

name: Layer 1 economy: 6 start Money, +2/turn, scaling every 5 rounds
body: Fixes dead opening; skills come online Turn 1. Accepted from Playtest 2 analysis.

name: Economy skills as actions
body: 2-slot scarcity makes this unworkable. Could be post-v1 expansion variant.

name: Flexible piece placement
body: Bundled with OQ-48; test after Stack A/B.

name: Focus / Charge timing & scope
body: Focus must come first; Charge retroactive. P2 mid-game ruling.

name: Focus on Move skills: caster chooses activation OR effect range
body: The +1 from Focus applies to either the activation range or the effect range - caster's choice at activation, not both. Resolves ambiguity for Move-skill / Focus interaction; preserves combo variety without making any single combo dominant.

name: Focus boosting self/adjacent skills
body: Can boost self→adjacent and adjacent→Range 2. Range and Injured calculated independently. Session 16 ruling.

name: Free pathing for movement (any route ≤ speed)
body: Cannot pass through any piece. Session 3 ruling.

name: Healing: no cap
body: Keeps it simple. Session 3 ruling.

name: Hex grid
body: Original Session 1 rejection was by omission: ADR-001 confirmed 'grid over card-fighter,' not 'square over hex.' Hex IS a grid variant. Reopened Session 8. Research needed before scheduling a test stack.

name: High-concept framing: 'Two minds, one puzzle' (Framing B)
body: Decided in ADR-004. See `adrs` table. Locks design intent: 2-player nature is load-bearing, combo legibility must work in both directions, asymmetry biased against. Design intent only - no immediate rule changes.

name: Injured: remove mechanical downsides (no speed cap, no Range −1) - Stack J → Stack M
body: Tests whether Injured's chassis volume (speed cap, Range −1, Range-modifier interactions, self/adjacent carve-out) pays for itself in game-feel terms. State still exists as HP-tracker. P4 partially confirmed: Niko named Injured as confusion source on first read; payoff felt thin to experienced player. Absorbed into Stack M Session 25.

name: Linked Movement-Action (move to act)
body: Unlinked preferred; likely superseded by AP system.

name: Minor / Major skill action cost
body: Pre-work needed: design ultimate-skill candidates first.

name: Money cap: none
body: No hoarding observed across P1, P2, P3. Naturally spends down. Closed from monitoring after P3.

name: Money income at start of each player's OWN turn
body: Resolves ambiguity - not end of round. Session 3 ruling.

name: Move-attack deals 1 damage (instead of 2)
body: P3: first Champion kill R11 vs P2's R26; standoff dissolved; combat feel 'Better/Much Better'. Accepted into baseline Session 15.

name: Move-Attack reframed as 'a Move that ends on an enemy tile'
body: Reworded Move Phase intro and Move-Attack opening to make move-attack unity explicit and plant skill-first thinking. Survival-stop rule strengthened with explicit attacker-speed cases (Guard speed 2 → 1 tile moved; Champion/King speed 1 → 0 tiles moved). Pure framing change - no mechanical change. BASELINE_VERSION bumped 2026-05-26.

name: Move-attack survival: attacker stops before target
body: Attacker occupies target tile only if target is removed. Session 3 ruling.

name: Skills that move pieces deal NO damage
body: General rule in Skill System section. P2 mid-game ruling.

name: No board (Direction B - card fighter)
body: Loses spatial skills (push/pull/swap). 'Just another card game.' Designer rejected.

name: No terrain effects
body: Confirmed overhead complexity; removed. Reversible as 'map variant' expansion.

name: Each piece moved at most once per Move Phase
body: Now explicit in all rule sheets. P2 mid-game ruling.

name: Skill path blocked by all pieces (ally + opponent)
body: Both players confirmed in P1. Ruling logged Session 3.

name: Path Idea 1 (only opponent pieces block)
body: Creates turtle meta - cluster all pieces, use skills from safety.

name: Path obstruction Idea 2 (only opponent Guards block)
body: Conditional on Stack A/B frustration data.

name: Performance-based Money gain
body: Forces single playstyle, constrains creative expression. Auto-economy is strategy-neutral. KPI problem - rewards symptoms, not systems.

name: Piece placement order - post-draft
body: Bundled with OQ-36; test after Stack A/B.

name: Pin / Threatened restriction
body: Restriction-as-reward. Backpocket; needs own stack.

name: Pole B prototype outcome → return to Pole A track
body: First Pole B digital prototype run surfaced three structural problems (Armor still felt mandatory; pure-reaction play; felt-PI broke). Designer call: return to Pole A as Active track with two sub-goals (onboard new players via pre-made loadouts; drastically shorten game to 30-60 min). Pole B paused, not abandoned; other Pole B variants remain alive.

name: Pole framing - parallel design tracks (Pole A pre-game-draft, Pole B per-turn-draft)
body: While core identity is unsettled, design proceeds along two parallel tracks rather than tweaking variables inside one rule set. Pole A = current game. Pole B = radical alternative (skills added during play; reusable while equipped; 12 equipped cap; shared action slots; no Money activation gate). Pairs with Principle 7. Pole B paused after P5 (Session 25) but direction not killed.

name: Pool draft variant
body: Test after Stack A/B accepted.

name: Range system clarification (self/adjacent/default)
body: All skills default to Range 2 unless text names 'self' or 'adjacent.' Range modifiers apply from default. Self/adjacent cannot be shifted inward by Range buffs. Injured penalty does not affect self/adjacent skills.

name: Restricted movement (straight-line only)
body: Layer 6 candidate - would make Move skills stronger. Now parked indefinitely.

name: Round 1 has no Money income (starting Money only)
body: Clarifies first turn. Session 3 ruling.

name: Information/scouting skill (reveal Money count)
body: Irrelevant in a perfect-information game.

name: Stack L - Pole B per-turn-draft prototype (consumable variant)
body: Session 25 (2026-06-21) after P5. First playtest surfaced three structural problems: Armor 3 still felt mandatory (cross-pole confirmation of OQ-11); pure-reaction play with no multi-turn planning (breaks Principle 4); felt-PI broke under combinatorial breadth even though formal-PI held. Pole A returns as Active. Pole B as a *direction* is paused, not killed.

name: Stack M bundled-deviation methodology justification
body: Stack M intentionally violates the Incremental Testing Methodology by bundling six simultaneous changes. Justified by Principle 7 (fundamental shifts while core unsettled), schedule cost of 6 sequential isolation stacks, prior independent validation of each component, and per-axis rollback routing that preserves attribution. Methodology recovers on the next stack.

name: Stack M combo-bonus scope expansion: any skill on a counter-loaded target
body: The Session 25 Stack M draft had movement-causing skills tick the target counter but reserved *bonus damage* for Strike hits only. Session 26 expanded this: any skill (Strike OR movement-causing) on a counter-loaded target deals +counter bonus damage. Unlocks damage strategies without Strike skills. Counter-tick rules unchanged. First rollback if dominant: revert to Session 25 draft (movement ticks counter, Strike-only deals bonus damage).

name: Stack M - Game Length Cut (six bundled changes)
body: Six simultaneous changes: (1) board 10×10→8×8; (2) Armor cap 3→2; (3) Injured penalties removed (still 2 HP tracker); (4) draw conditions removed entirely; (5) Steal cost 3→4 both Modes; (6) Multi-Champion Combo Bonus also ticks on movement-causing skills (Tempest push, Hook pull, Blast push, Shove, Swap when relocating enemy). Hypothesis: single coordinated cut delivers 30-60 min length + single-climax shape (Principle 8) without breaking combo fantasy. Each lever maps to a specific compounding curve in the 12-economy map. Per-axis rollback routing in the rule sheet handles each failure mode surgically. Session 26 expanded the combo lever further: bonus damage also applies to any skill on a counter-loaded target, not only Strikes.

name: Starting player bid (hidden Money auction)
body: No first-player advantage observed. If surfaces, use Go-style komi instead.

name: Blade Tempest does NOT affect caster
body: Only target takes 1 damage. P2 mid-game ruling.

name: Terrain effects (Water/Forest/Plains/Mountains)
body: Confirmed overhead complexity; removed. Reversible as 'map variant' expansion.

name: 3 Move actions per turn (vs current 2)
body: May be superseded by AP system (Stack G).

name: Unified AP system (3 AP/turn) - Stack G
body: Cleaner decisions; merges Move + Skill phases into one action pool. Stack G is dormant.

name: Unlinked Move + Skill phases
body: Move Phase and Skill Phase are unlinked. Intuitive and appreciated by both players in P1.

name: YINSH-inspired capture penalty
body: Creates asymmetric cost - if one player runs out of Guards, only the other player pays the penalty. Punishes playing correctly.

name: Zone/lane system (Direction C - spatial hybrid)
body: Direction A+ chosen instead; grid preserved.
